newsitem.title: USA: U.S. condemns IRA killing of two policemen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. condemns IRA killing of two policemen.

text.p: The White House on Monday condemned the killing of two Northern Ireland policemen by Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas, calling it outrageous and cowardly.

"The United States government too is outraged by the callous murder of two policemen in Northern Ireland," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters. "The IRA has claimed responsibility for what is ultimately an outrageous act of cowardice, an outrageous act of terrorism."
IRA guerrillas killed the policemen in an ambush in the town of Lurgan, throwing the halting Northern Ireland peace process into turmoil.
McCurry also called on pro-British Loyalist guerrillas, who have maintained a shaky truce since October 1994, not to retaliate for the killings.

"The United States government of course will continue to call on them to honour their own ceasefire and to avoid acts of retaliation because that sends you into the downward spiral that is all too familiar to the people of Ireland," he said.
Asked if the United States expected to continue to have contacts with Sinn Fein, the White House spokesman hinted at growing U.S. frustration with the political wing of the IRA.
"We will continue the contacts that we believe are helpful to the process, but sooner or later it becomes clear who is willing to help the process and who is not," McCurry said.
The IRA shattered its 18-month-long ceasefire with a bombing in London in February 1996.
